[binding.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/binding.md) is written and committed on `worktree/qf-2`, not merged. Writing it turned up one real bug in the template code, which is now fixed and tested.

### 📏 Measured: 1,000 rows `binding/measure.mjs`
Each row has 10 cells; 3 of them are live, and one of those is a value every row shares. Headless Chromium, real spans, median of 3 runs:

| | update the shared value | change a value no cell shows | listeners | memory (JS heap) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| re-render | 38 ms | 36 ms | 0 | 0.5 MB |
| a Property per cell | 7.9 ms | 0 | 10,000 | 3.2 MB |
| **lazy (built)** | 8.1 ms | 0 | 3,000 | 1.3 MB |
| Item `change` | 4.4 ms | 0.03 ms | 2,000 | 1.0 MB |

- Binding is about 5 times faster per update than redrawing everything.
- The lazy way uses 2.4 times less memory than a Property per cell.
- Item's `change` event did as well as lazy Properties. I don't know yet why its update was faster in the browser; the node run shows no gap.
- Every approach went back to exactly 0 listeners after the views were dropped.
- The raw output is in [results.txt](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/12/session-87bec773/page-templates/binding/results.txt).

---

### 🐛 Fixed: `class Template extends Page` `core/Page/Template/Template.js`
- ✅ **The bug:** when a middle clone overrode or reset a value, its own clones kept showing the old one. `set` and `unset` now redraw every clone, at any depth, that still reads that value through it.
- ✅ **New, per your point 2:**
  - `dispose()` — a clone that dies removes its own clones, views and listeners.
  - `copy()` — a hard copy with no link back to the template.
  - `overrides(prefix)` — lists what a clone overrides, for one property or a whole section.
- ✅ **Tests:** `Property.test.mjs` 24/24; the new `Template.test.mjs` 14/14, run headless against qf-2.
- ⚠️ **Not built, design only in the doc:** `Field`, `Property.of(item, name)`, a list field, and the `={path}` / `={expr}` syntax.
